## Teaching points

1. SJS/TEN starts 4–28 days (usually 1–3 weeks) after a new drug; high-risk culprits include sulfonamide antibiotics, aromatic anticonvulsants, lamotrigine, allopurinol, oxicam NSAIDs and nevirapine.
2. The spectrum is defined by detached or detachable skin: SJS under 10% BSA, SJS/TEN overlap 10–30%, TEN over 30%; mucosal involvement is usual.
3. Stop the culprit immediately: continuing trimethoprim–sulfamethoxazole after the first erythema allowed progression here.
4. Calculate SCORTEN within 24 hours and manage extensive detachment in a burn centre or ICU, with early ophthalmology, gynaecology or urology and dermatology input.
5. The trigger was avoidable: asymptomatic bacteriuria in a healthy non-pregnant woman should not be treated.
